newsitem.title: USA: Grand jury to probe border shooting by Marines.
newsitem.headline: Grand jury to probe border shooting by Marines.

text.p: A grand jury convenes on Wednesday to decide whether to charge a group of Marines in the shooting death of a high school student while they were on an anti-narcotics operation on the U.S.-Mexico border.
Esequiel Hernandez, 18, was shot dead by one of a group of four Marines in the tiny Texas border town of Redford on May 20.

The Marines, who were part of the Task Force Six military unit which helps local law enforcement agencies in the war on drugs, said Hernandez opened fire on them first and that he was shot him in self defence.
But Hernandez' family insists he was herding some family goats and only carried his .22-calibre rifle to scare away wild dogs.

A spokesperson for the District Attorney's office in Fort Stockton said on Tuesday that the state grand jury would convene in Marfa early on Wednesday and would hear testimony from senior officers at Task Force Six, the U.S. Border Patrol, the Texas Rangers and from Hernandez' relatives.
It was not clear how long the grand jury probe would last.
Investigators from the Texas Rangers have said the evidence in the case does not point to self defence because the Marines apparently tracked Hernandez and then shot him.
They said the teenager was not given any medical aid until an ambulance arrived at the spot almost half an hour after the shooting.
But Air Force Col. Henry Hungerbeeler, who was in charge of the Marines, said on Tuesday that the Border Patrol bears some responsibility in the case because it was slow in arriving at the scene.

He said the Marines called the Border Patrol and told agents they had been fired upon. Hungerbeeler said agents, according to a written agreement, should have arrived within 15 minutes but instead took 38 minutes.
Hungerbeeler also said using the military in civilian operations like drug surveillance was problematic.

"The military would like to get out of this job," he said. "A major concern of the Defence Department now is how do we protect our people from unfair prosecution arising out of their attempts to fulfil their mission."
After the shooting, the use of Task Force Six units was suspended in almost every Border Patrol sector in Texas and New Mexico.
